items.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019
items.q: And it’s like Sarah Vaughan. We used to call Sarah “the divine Miss Vaughan.” She has that in her music too.

ctx.x: That was Dizzy 24 hours a day. I never saw Dizzy ever depressed. Ever. He totally escaped neurosis. And we lived, like he would stay at my parents’ house, and often times I stayed with his relatives. And so I observed Dizzy waking up in the morning and then — he was like that all the time. I never saw him ever depressed. And I asked him once, “Man how do you do that?” He said, “I decided early on in life to become a creature of joy.” And I asked him once also, “What is your music about?” And he said, “Absolute ©…

love for every man, woman, child, gay and lesbian on the planet.” And Dizzy had — if you ever listen to an album called “The Man From Monterey” he plays “The Shadow of Your Smile.” I couldn’t play it for two years after he died. It’s unexplainable beauty. And he only plays one chorus, the melody chorus. But it’s so gorgeous man, it’s like — what is this? It’s coming from some other place. And he had that. It’s divine.
